correctness.rationale: The positive global solution and the pathwise identity \(\log(I/Z)=\int[(1-\alpha)\beta S+H-\eta]\,dt\) are derived under bounded adapted controls. Full suppression \(\alpha=1,\ \eta=H\) attains equality as entire processes, forcing simultaneous sharp stochastic ordering for terminal and supremum events. Gaussian evaluation, the verified drifted-Brownian first-passage density, its antiderivative and infinite-horizon limit give the exact probabilities. Total-variation discrepancy is proved by the measurable complement of bounded support. Four independent numerical density integrations check the finite-time formula; they are not substituted for the proof.

originality.rationale: The precise joint claim—the attainable all-policy stochastic lower envelope, first-passage peak law, and finite-domain total-variation floor for persistent infected-only noise—is not contained in the motivating full-text Fokker-Planck study, which optimizes a different finite-domain PDE and uses transmission-proportional numerical noise. The earlier stochastic SIS transmission-noise model has a conserved total and a different diffusion. A 2026 exact first-passage SIS paper concerns a finite-state jump chain. A previously published same-source covariance note addresses driver correlation, not peak risk. Ordinary Brownian first-passage theory supplies a standard proof tool, not the applied all-control result. These comparisons are best-knowledge claims with specified residual access risks.

value.rationale: Hospital-capacity exceedance is an explicit mathematical goal of the motivating work. The claim supplies simultaneous optimal finite-time crossing probabilities and a nonzero power-law eventual-peak risk for every finite removal capacity, uniformly over all bounded adapted controls. A numerical example shows peak overflow probability 0.189799 versus only 0.040654 terminal exceedance. The same sharp Gaussian terminal bound yields a provable positive total-variation discrepancy for any bounded-support law approximating this diffusion. Unlike a basic positivity check, these are exact natural risk quantities with implications for stochastic control objectives and bounded-domain modeling; they are conditional on the specified persistent noise and make no empirical prediction.
